subject: Emotions
title: Information Overload
description: A micro-lesson that makes Information Overload usable.

hook.text: The average person sees 10,000 ads per day. Each one tries to surprise you. Your brain is drowning in novelty.

buildup.text: Alvin Toffler predicted 'future shock' in 1970: a society changing so fast that surprise becomes chronic stress.

discovery.text: Chronic novelty triggers cortisol. The brain evolved for occasional surprise, not 24/7 notification pings.

twist.text: Digital detox works because it removes surprise triggers. Boredom is actually your brain's recovery mode.

climax.text: The attention economy profits from surprise. Your overwhelm is their revenue model.

punchline.text: Too much surprise isn't exciting. It's exhausting.

quiz.question: Who predicted 'future shock' from rapid societal change?
